title: Health insurance — why it matters before your first big bill
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Health insurance pays hospital bills so one illness does not wipe out your savings. Even if your employer provides group cover, get a personal policy too, because group cover ends when you leave the job. Key terms: sum insured (the maximum the insurer pays in a year), waiting period (before pre-existing conditions are covered, often 2–4 years), co-pay (the share you pay), room-rent limit (a low limit can reduce your payout proportionally), and cashless network hospitals. Buy young, when premiums are lowest and you can declare no pre-existing conditions. A cover of ₹5–10 lakh is a sensible starting point for a young adult in a metro, topped up later with a cheap super top-up. Read the exclusions, and always disclose existing conditions honestly.
summary_hinglish: Health insurance bade hospital bill se savings bachata hai. Company ka group cover job chhodne par khatam ho jaata hai, isliye personal policy bhi lo. Waiting period, co-pay, room-rent limit dekho. Jaldi lo kyunki premium kam hota hai; shuruaat ₹5-10 lakh ke cover se ho sakti hai.
summary_hi: हेल्थ इंश्योरेंस बड़े अस्पताल बिल से आपकी बचत बचाता है। कंपनी का ग्रुप कवर नौकरी छोड़ने पर खत्म हो जाता है, इसलिए निजी पॉलिसी भी लें। वेटिंग पीरियड, को-पे और रूम-रेंट सीमा देखें। जल्दी लें क्योंकि प्रीमियम कम होता है; ₹5-10 लाख के कवर से शुरुआत कर सकते हैं।
